title: WPMS/1546/2019 of HITESH BALOONI Vs HEMWATI NANDAN BAHUGUNA GARHWAL UNIVERSITY

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1546 of 2019
Hitesh Balooni ..........Petitioner

Versus
Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, Srinagar &
others ...Respondents
Present:- Mr. Sanjay Bhatt, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Advocate for respondent nos. 1 and 2.

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 Petitioner had taken admission for Bachelor of
Science Programme in DAV (PG) College, Dehradun for 2015-
2018 batch. The minimum credit for qualifying in the fifth
semester was 132 credit marks, but the petitioner obtained
118 credit marks and he was short of 14 credit marks. Hence,
he is not technically a graduate. Meanwhile, the petitioner
took admission in B.P.Ed., course in Bharateeya Vidyapeeth
Deemed University, Pune. Now on a special drive initiated by
the HNB Garhwal University any candidate who had failed in
fifth semester and was short of "not more than 12 credit
points", could appear again and clear the semester.
2. Evidently, though the petitioner was not eligible
for this, as he had 14 credit points short (and not just 12 as
required), but nevertheless, he had applied and surprisingly
admission was also given to him by the concerned College
which is DAV (PG) College, Dehradun. The petitioner gave his
examination fee etc, which has been accepted and the

2
petitioner appeared in the examination. Evidently, he has also
passed in the examination but the University is not giving the
degree and mark-sheet to the petitioner on the ground that
the petitioner in the first place was not eligible to appear in the
examination as he was short of 14 credit points and only those
candidates could have appeared who were short by maximum
12 credit points.
3. This is in fact true that apparently the petitioner
was not qualified to appear in the examination, yet he applied
for the same and under what circumstances he has also been
given admission by the concerned College needs to be
examined, but considering now that he has appeared in the
examination and subsequently passed the examination,
though no interference is being called for by this Court in the
matter, however, the writ petition stands disposed with a
direction to the petitioner to move a representation before the
Vice-Chancellor of the University, who may consider the same
sympathetically, as the career of a student is involved, as
expeditiously as possible.
4. Meanwhile, the concerned College which has
taken the examination of the petitioner in violation of the law
must be given show cause notice by the concerned authority
and the State Government so that these incidents are not
repeated in future.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 08.08.2019
Ankit/
